summary: IDS feed s168_triple is degraded: 17.4% duplicates, 20.6% one-way TCP sessions (IDS requires both directions), and 2.09 Gbps microbursts exceeding 1 Gbps port capacity (209%). Stateful inspection is impaired and overload will cause drops/missed detections.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker not aggregating both directions of flows to same IDS tool port - likely asymmetric TAP/SPAN feeds or per-direction load-balancing without symmetric hashing. 29 of 141 TCP sessions (20.6%) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for stateful TCP reassembly and attack detection; one-way flows cause incomplete sessions, missed exploits, and high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate complementary directions with symmetric 5-tuple hashing so both client->server and server->client for each session land on this same IDS port, restoring stateful visibility.

findings.root_cause: Microburst traffic peaking at 2.09 Gbps in 1ms intervals overwhelms the 1 Gbps IDS ingress port (209% of capacity, 5 overloaded intervals). Likely insufficient capacity planning or no load-balancing/shaping on broker egress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port oversubscription causes buffer drops before analysis; IDS will miss packets during bursts, blind to attacks and unable to reassemble sessions, degrading detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2-3 IDS ports/instances with 5-tuple load balancing to keep per-port utilization under 80% of 1 Gbps and absorb 2+ Gbps bursts without drops.

findings.root_cause: 17.4% duplicate packets (419 of 2411) indicates same traffic mirrored from multiple SPANs/TAPs aggregated without deduplication on the packet broker, or SPAN duplication from overlapping mirror sessions.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates waste 17% of IDS 1 Gbps budget (worsening overload), inflate flow counts, skew analytics, and can trigger false-positive retransmission/anomaly alerts while reducing effective inspection capacity.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-based deduplication (packet hash window ~10ms) to strip duplicates before IDS, reclaiming bandwidth and preventing duplicate-induced detection errors.
